memories.content: The user keeps a small table fan beside the bedroom window.
On a day the user drank coffee late in the afternoon, they could not fall asleep until dawn.
On a day the user drank coffee before 2 p.m., they fell asleep at their usual time.
On a tired day, the user ate dinner out and postponed even washing the dishes after returning home.
In the same week, on a day the user made simple noodles at home, they rested immediately after the meal.
On a night the window was left open, street noise woke the user twice.
On a night the table fan was running, the user was not too warm even with the window closed.
The user's father prefers to have coffee available after dinner and believes it will not cause a sleep problem.
When making a sleep-related suggestion, do not treat one or two records as a general lifestyle habit.
The user tends to go to bed much later after drinking coffee late in the afternoon.
The user recorded a family dinner in the calendar for the final week of November.
In a crowded restaurant, the user had to ask several times for orders to be repeated, interrupting the flow of conversation.
When the user held the next gathering at their father's home, they continued the conversation on the sofa after the meal.
At a gathering with loud music prepared by their older sister, the user developed a headache and went outside briefly.
On a day the user held a yard barbecue with their younger brother, the open space dispersed the sound and made conversation easier.
After seeing a message that their maternal aunt would arrive at 5 p.m., the user delayed meal preparation by an hour.
On a day the user waited without knowing their maternal uncle's arrival time, they reheated the food twice.
The user's maternal uncle considers it easier to time his departure when he knows the family meal's start time in advance.
Before scheduling a family meal, confirm the attendees' arrival times and the location with the user.
Available restaurant reservation times may diminish quickly during the year-end gathering season.

analysis.overview: The frames contain separate operational domains with no justified shared claim: the reference covers sleep, coffee timing, bedroom airflow, and post-meal recovery, while the compared frame covers family-gathering planning, timing, venues, and sound conditions.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories provide observations and a tendency statement that split one caffeine-timing and sleep claim; the compared frame contains no counterpart.
relations.summary: Coffee timing is associated with the user’s sleep timing, with late-afternoon coffee linked to much later sleep and coffee before 2 p.m. linked to usual sleep.

relations.reason: The two reference-side episodes split one claim about minimizing post-meal effort, while the compared frame does not address the user’s recovery after ordinary dinners.
relations.summary: On low-energy days, the user rested promptly or deferred household activity after dinner.

relations.reason: The setup and two nighttime observations jointly describe one bedroom airflow and noise-management context absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: The bedroom fan-and-window setup involves a tradeoff between cooling and street-noise disruption, with the fan allowing the window to remain closed without excessive warmth.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided preference and belief about evening coffee, not a claim about family-meal logistics or venue conditions.
relations.summary: The user’s father wants coffee available after dinner and believes it will not impair sleep.

relations.reason: This evidentiary guardrail is independently useful and has no corresponding instruction in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Sleep-related suggestions should not generalize a lifestyle habit from only one or two records.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided scheduled-event fact with no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: A family dinner is recorded in the calendar for the final week of November.

relations.reason: These compared-side episodes split one claim about how gathering environments shape auditory comfort and conversation; the reference bedroom-noise observations govern a different operational setting.
relations.summary: Gathering venues and sound conditions affected conversation continuity and physical comfort, with crowded or loud settings causing difficulty and open or home settings supporting easier conversation.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories describe complementary effects of family timing coordination, a subject absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: Advance knowledge of relatives’ arrival or meal timing affects food preparation and departure planning, while uncertainty can cause repeated reheating.

relations.reason: This operational scheduling instruction is independently useful and has no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Before scheduling a family meal, the user should be asked to confirm attendee arrival times and the location.

relations.reason: This seasonal planning constraint appears only in the compared frame and is distinct from the recorded November event and confirmation policy.
relations.summary: Restaurant reservation availability may shrink quickly during the year-end gathering season.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame records gathering plans, venue and sound experiences, arrival-time coordination, scheduling confirmation needs, and seasonal reservation pressure.
reports.reference_only: The reference records coffee-related sleep patterns and cautions, bedroom heat-and-noise observations, low-energy post-dinner behavior, and the father’s view of evening coffee.
